cleared.check: Do reth v2.11.0 (Ethereum endpoint), op-reth v2.8.1 (OP Mainnet) and op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1 (Unichain, Ink, Soneium) put the alloy-primitives keccak cache in front of KECCAK256, and with which versions.
cleared.result: Yes for all three, by default, with the same text cycle 10 read for Tempo. reth bin/reth/Cargo.toml lines 88-99 list keccak-cache-global in default and lines 135-139 forward it to alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global. op-reth rust/op-reth/bin/Cargo.toml line 38 lists it in default and lines 68-72 forward it through reth-optimism-cli and reth-optimism-node, whose own feature (op-reth/crates/cli/Cargo.toml lines 82-85, crates/node/Cargo.toml lines 129-132) sets alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global. The three lockfiles pin alloy-primitives 1.7.3 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (reth Cargo.lock line 4365, op-reth v2.8.1 line 5259, v2.9.0-rc.1 line 5260). The endpoints answered web3_clientVersion with reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc, op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 (and an unversioned op-reth dev build on OP Mainnet) and op-reth/v2.9.0-rc.1-72fcf947. No mismatch appeared in the bucket test of this cycle on any of the five.

cleared.check: Does Base v1.5.6 enable the keccak cache, through which edge, and is its alloy-primitives version a text not yet read.
cleared.result: It is enabled by default. bin/node/Cargo.toml line 31 lists keccak-cache-global in default and line 33 forwards it to base-execution-cli, whose feature (crates/execution/cli/Cargo.toml lines 113-115) sets base-node-core and reth-node-core (base/reth tag base-v2.5.2.11, crates/node/core/Cargo.toml line 5: alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global). The lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.1 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (Cargo.lock line 9776). The keccak_cache.rs of the 1.6.1 crate is byte identical to that of 1.7.3 (diff of the two crates from static.crates.io printed nothing), so the cache text is the one already read: a OnceLock holding fixed_cache::Cache::new(1 << 17), EPOCHS false, STATS only with keccak-cache-stats, which no Base manifest read sets. The endpoint reported reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/.../base/v1.5.6, and the bucket test found no mismatch.

cleared.check: Does X Layer (xlayer-reth v0.0.7) enable the keccak cache, and does its combination of alloy-primitives 1.6.0 with fixed-cache 0.1.10, which neither Tempo nor Arc runs, behave as the read versions do.
cleared.result: It is enabled, although bin/node/Cargo.toml line 75 has default = [] and its own asm-keccak feature does not touch the cache. The edge is the reth crate: bin/node/Cargo.toml line 28 takes reth.workspace, the workspace Cargo.toml line 89 pins reth from okx/reth rev 81573d2c without default-features = false, and that crate's bin/reth/Cargo.toml lists keccak-cache-global in default (lines 85-91) and forwards it to alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global (lines 119-122). The lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.0 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (Cargo.lock line 3767). The keccak_cache.rs of 1.6.0 is byte identical to that of 1.5.7 (Arc's text): a static cache built by fixed_cache::static_cache! with COUNT 1 << 17 (line 13), EPOCHS false (line 20), inputs of 0 bytes or more than 87 bytes skip the cache (lines 23-26). In fixed-cache 0.1.10 the static_cache! macro builds every bucket with Bucket::new(), which sets tag 0 and zeroed data (lib.rs line 583-585), so the first lookup of any bucket sees a key of length 0 that never equals a nonempty input. The get and insert paths are those of the next item. The endpoint reported reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/.../xlayer/v0.0.7, and the bucket test found no mismatch.

cleared.check: Reread of the fixed-cache 0.1.10 get and insert paths that every cache user in this list runs: key equality, lock protocol, epochs, and what a reader sees while a writer is inserting.
cleared.result: No path returns a hash for another input. calc (lib.rs lines 527-540) takes bucket = hash & (capacity - 1) and tag = hash & !(capacity - 1). Key and value are Copy types, so NEEDS_DROP is false and ALIVE_BIT is never set, and EPOCHS is false in both alloy texts, so the epoch bits are not used. The tag never has bit 0 set because the low 17 bits are masked off. get_inner (lines 322-350) succeeds only if a Relaxed load of the bucket state equals the tag exactly and a compare-exchange from tag to tag | LOCKED_BIT with Acquire succeeds (try_lock_ret, lines 593-606). While a writer holds the bucket the state carries LOCKED_BIT, so a reader's expected value does not match and it returns None and hashes the input itself. Under the lock the reader returns the stored value only if key.equivalent holds, which for [u8] against Key compares the slice of length len, so length and every byte must match (alloy keccak_cache.rs line 88 in 1.6.0, line 128 in 1.6.1). insert_inner (lines 389-439) takes the lock with expected None, which fails if the bucket is locked, writes key and value together, and releases with a Release store of the new tag (unlock, line 613). An ABA case in which another key with the same 64 bit hash replaces the entry between the reader's load and its compare-exchange leaves a reader that fails the equality test and recomputes. The value stored is imp(input) computed for the same input as the key (get_or_try_insert_with_ref, lines 506-524). This build has no lock-free read path: the string LOCK_FREE does not occur in lib.rs.

cleared.check: Does the KECCAK256 opcode go through the cache in each interpreter these nodes run, and does the hashing of storage keys for the state trie go through it as well.
cleared.result: Both do where the feature is on, and only the opcode result reaches the PoolManager. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer), 42.0.0 (Base) and 43.0.2 (op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1) implement KECCAK256 in instructions/system.rs lines 18-40 as KECCAK_EMPTY for length 0, else primitives::keccak256 over the memory slice, and revm-primitives 24.0.1, 42.0.0 and 43.0.0 re-export alloy_primitives::keccak256 (lib.rs lines 39-41). evm2 at rev 66687c18, which reth v2.11.0 runs, calls alloy_primitives::keccak256 in interpreter/instructions/crypto.rs lines 2 and 14. alloy-primitives utils/mod.rs lines 147-150 route keccak256 through keccak_cache::compute when keccak-cache-global is set. reth's trie hashes account and slot keys with the same function (crates/trie/common/src/key.rs line 16, hashed_state.rs line 55). Those hashed keys feed the state root. SLOAD and SSTORE look up the plain slot word, so a wrong trie key hash would give a wrong state root and a halted or forked node, while the slot the PoolManager reads and writes comes only from the KECCAK256 opcode result.

cleared.check: Bucket collision test: KECCAK256 of 1 to 88 byte inputs chosen to share a bucket of the cache, sent interleaved so each lookup evicts the previous entry, in parallel requests, against the Python keccak.
cleared.result: No wrong hash on any of the 14 endpoints. The bucket index is hash & (2^17 - 1) with hash = rapidhash_v3_micro_inline::<false, false>(input, RapidSecrets::seed(0)) (alloy keccak_cache.rs lines 48-60 in 1.6.0, 88-100 in 1.6.1; fixed-cache calc; rapidhash 4.4.1 and 4.5.1 v3/rapid_const.rs lines 236-310, which are identical in the two versions). The script transcribes that function in Python. A pool of 34,400 inputs (300 random inputs of each length 1 to 88, 3,000 delta-slot inputs of address word then currency word as CurrencyDelta.sol builds them, 2,000 mapping-slot inputs and 3,000 position-key inputs of 58 bytes as Position.sol builds them) fell into 3,723 buckets that hold two or more inputs. 3,528 of those buckets mix lengths and 1,556 hold a PoolManager-shaped input. Each bucket was sent as A B A B A B plus A without its last byte, A with an extra zero byte and A again. 300 extra groups put 87 byte inputs, which are cached, next to their 88 byte extensions, which skip the cache. That is 36,059 hashes per round, in chunks of 500 records, four requests at a time, three rounds per endpoint, 108,177 hashes per endpoint, all as specified. World Chain and Celo do not enable the cache by their manifests and served as controls. Polygon's eth_call does not reach Bor's block-import cache (next item). The transcription of rapidhash could not be compared with the compiled crate because building a Rust harness was not permitted in this session. If it is wrong, the inputs still exercise the cache at random buckets, and every result was checked.

cleared.check: Do World Chain v2.8.2 and Celo's celo-reth enable keccak-cache-global.
cleared.result: Neither does, as far as the manifests read show. World Chain: bin/world-chain/Cargo.toml line 40 has default = ["jemalloc"], the workspace takes reth-node-core, reth-cli-util and all reth-optimism crates with default-features = false (Cargo.toml lines 132, 177, 185-197), and the Dockerfile builds with FEATURES="jemalloc" (line 37). Its lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.1 and fixed-cache 0.1.10, so if the cache were turned on it would run the text already read. Celo: forno answered with reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, which matches the reth-node-core patch to celo-org/reth rev 74cc8bbc in celo-kona tag celo/reth-v1.0.10 (Cargo.toml line 466). The celo-reth crate (crates/celo-reth/Cargo.toml line 146) has default = ["std"] and no cache feature, its Dockerfile builds -p celo-reth with no features, and the patched reth-optimism-node at celo-org/optimism b08a8d0 has default = ["reth-codec"] (line 110). Its lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.0 with fixed-cache 0.1.8, the versions read for Arc. In one of three requests forno answered from a different backend, Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 (go1.24.13), which is a geth-family node with no alloy cache. No full cargo feature resolution was run, so a feature set by a crate outside those read cannot be excluded. The bucket test matched on both.

cleared.check: Does the public MegaETH stateless validator compile the keccak cache.
cleared.result: No. Its Cargo.lock (megaeth-labs/stateless-validator, main branch as fetched on 2026-11-24, version 2.1.0, mega-evm tag v1.7.3, revm 40.0.3, ruint 1.17.2) contains no fixed-cache package, and the alloy-primitives 1.6.0 entry does not list it as a dependency, so keccak-cache-global cannot be on in any build of that lock. The RPC node, mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc, is not public, and the bucket test on it found no mismatch.

cleared.check: Bor v2.11.1, which the Polygon publicnode endpoint reports (bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private), adds its own cache of 64 byte KECCAK256 results. Can it return a hash for another input.
cleared.result: No. opKeccak256 (core/vm/instructions.go lines 259-290) uses the cache only when the input is exactly 64 bytes and evm.Config.Keccak256Cache is set. It copies all 64 bytes into a [64]byte key, and on a miss it hashes the data and stores (key, hash). Keccak256Cache is BoundedCache[[64]byte, common.Hash] (keccak_cache.go line 26), a sync.Map keyed by the whole array, written with LoadOrStore so an entry is never replaced, and capped at 65,536 entries, past which Store does nothing (bounded_cache.go lines 28-59). The cache is created per block in ProcessBlock (blockchain.go lines 1276-1288, 1328-1329 and 1348) and given to the prefetcher and the BlockSTM V2 workers. Speculative runs can only add pairs of an input and its true hash, which are right in any later run. eth_call does not set the field, so the bucket test on Polygon could not reach it. The 64 byte inputs it serves are the delta slots and mapping slots of src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-14 and src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:69-70. The same block adds an ecrecover result cache (core/vm/evm.go lines 57-87). The PoolManager source has no ecrecover or staticcall (grep of src/), so that cache is outside its path.

cleared.check: Do the other geth-family clients put a cache in front of KECCAK256.
cleared.result: Not in the sources read. BSC v1.8.2 (the version the BSC endpoint reports) computes crypto.Keccak256Hash(data) on every call (core/vm/instructions.go lines 232-243). The OffchainLabs go-ethereum master branch, which Nitro builds on, and the ava-labs libevm main branch, which avalanchego 1.15.3 builds on, reset a per-interpreter Keccak state and hash the data on every call (instructions.go lines 236-246 in both). For Nitro and libevm these are branch heads, not the commits the endpoints run.

cleared.check: L-633: X Layer pins ruint 1.18.0 and Base ruint 1.19.0, inside RUSTSEC-2026-0220. Does every SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE handler of the revm-interpreter they pin clamp the amount before calling ruint, and does any precompile or handler they run call a ruint shift with an unclamped amount.
cleared.result: The handlers clamp, and the other code read has no unclamped shift. The advisory says the shifted values of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr were right and only the overflow flag was wrong, and that wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr took the amount modulo 2^32. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer) and 42.0.0 (Base) convert the amount with as_usize_saturated (macros.rs lines 122-126) and call << and >> (which are wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr) and arithmetic_shr only when the amount is below 256, else return 0 or the sign fill. BYTE indexes only below 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). SIGNEXTEND shifts by at most 247 (arithmetic.rs lines 126-136). A Python transcription of the ruint 1.19.0 u256 paths of wrapping_shl, wrapping_shr and arithmetic_shr (bits.rs lines 437-467, 573-603, 612-623) matched the EVM definition on 509,184 cases covering every amount 0 to 255. A grep of revm-precompile 36.0.3 and 42.0.1, op-revm 20.0.0, revm-handler 20.0.3 and 42.0.1, alloy-evm 0.36.0 and 0.38.0 and alloy-op-evm 0.32.0 finds no call to a wrapping, overflowing, checked or saturating shift, and every << or >> with a U256 operand uses a constant amount. Base's crates/common/evm sources (precompiles/mod.rs, handler.rs, evm.rs and the other 11 files) shift only by constants. base-common-evm2 is in the Base workspace, but no package in the Base lockfile depends on it. The xlayer-reth crates directory has no EVM or precompile crate (builder, chainspec, flashblocks, intercept, legacy-rpc, monitor, rcs-filter, rpc, tests, version), and those crates were not read line by line.

leads.question: With which FEATURES build argument is the conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 image that serves Zora built? Its binary crate has keccak-cache-global with no default features (crates/bin/Cargo.toml lines 46-49), and the Dockerfile passes --features="$FEATURES" (line 75).
leads.why: If the feature is on, the cache text is alloy-primitives 1.7.3 with fixed-cache 0.1.10, which reads clean. The open part is only whether Zora runs it. The bucket test matched on the Zora endpoint either way.

leads.question: Does mega-reth v2.2.3, the closed MegaETH RPC and sequencer client, enable keccak-cache-global or a cache of its own in front of KECCAK256, and with which fixed-cache version?
leads.why: The public stateless validator has no cache, so a cache in the sequencer that returned a wrong slot would make the validator reject the block rather than accept it silently. The configuration cannot be read from outside.

leads.question: Compile the rapidhash 4.4.1 v3 micro function and compare it with the Python transcription in keccak_buckets.py, so the bucket collision test is known to hit the buckets it aims at.
leads.why: Building the harness was not permitted in this session. Without it the test exercises eviction at random buckets rather than at designed collisions.

leadResults.answer: keccak-cache-global is on by default in reth v2.11.0 (bin/reth/Cargo.toml lines 88-99 and 135-139), op-reth v2.8.1 and v2.9.0-rc.1 (op-reth/bin/Cargo.toml lines 38 and 68-72), Base v1.5.6 (bin/node/Cargo.toml lines 31 and 33, through base-execution-cli and reth-node-core) and xlayer-reth v0.0.7 (through its dependency on the okx/reth reth crate with default features, whose default list includes the feature). It is off by default in world-chain v2.8.2 and celo-reth (celo-kona celo/reth-v1.0.10). For conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 it is an optional feature whose image build flags are not public. The MegaETH stateless validator does not compile fixed-cache. The versions are alloy-primitives 1.7.3 with fixed-cache 0.1.10 for reth, op-reth and conduit, 1.6.1 with 0.1.10 for Base and World Chain, 1.6.0 with 0.1.10 for X Layer, and 1.6.0 with 0.1.8 for Celo. 1.6.1 has the same keccak_cache.rs as 1.7.3, and 1.6.0 the same as 1.5.7, so no new cache text exists. fixed-cache 0.1.10 was reread: exact length and byte equality under an Acquire compare-exchange lock, no epochs, no lock-free reads, and a reader that meets a locked bucket recomputes. revm's KECCAK256 and evm2's both call alloy_primitives::keccak256, and reth's trie key hashing does as well but only affects the state root. 108,177 bucket-colliding hashes per endpoint on 14 endpoints, including Bor's own 64 byte cache noted separately, all matched.

revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer, ruint 1.18.0) and 42.0.0 (Base, ruint 1.19.0) clamp SHL, SHR and SAR to amounts below 256 and BYTE to indices below 32 before calling ruint (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). The faulty overflow flags are never read, and the modulo 2^32 truncation cannot occur below 256. The ruint 1.19.0 u256 shift paths transcribed to Python match the EVM on 509,184 cases. No shift with an unclamped amount appears in revm-precompile, op-revm, revm-handler, alloy-evm, alloy-op-evm or Base's evm crate as pinned. Base's evm2 crate is not linked into any package of the lockfile.
